John Donne, Poetry.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/john-donne/poetry

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- John Donne, the author, died 1631.

First publication of the text used: between 1611 and 1669 (SE colophon: 'Poetry was compiled from poetry published between 1611 and 1669 by John Donne.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the edition's rights statement (quoted below) says the text is in the US public domain. The text was first published between 1611 and 1669, so the 95-year US term from the latest first publication ended by 1 January 1765.
- Country of origin: the facts do not name the country of first publication. Every person named above died in 1631 or earlier, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less, whatever that country is.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: Poetry was compiled from poetry published between 1611 and 1669 by John Donne.
- Wikidata Q140412 (John Donne), P570 = 1631-03-31 and 1631; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Donne
